item.title: Trump claims Iran doing "everything they can" to drive up oil prices ahead of midterms
item.description: President Trump claimed that Iran is intentionally driving up oil prices ahead of the U.S. midterm election after the country took responsibility for striking oil tankers near the Strait of Hormuz. CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean has more.

item.title: Rep. Dan Crenshaw calls for restoration of Ukraine's SpaceX satellite access
item.description: Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are calling for the full restoration of Ukraine's access to the SpaceX satellite service, including Republican Rep. Dan Crenshaw of Texas. Crenshaw joins "The Takeout" with his perspective.

item.title: How Trump's immigration crackdown may reshape Republican voting in Texas
item.description: President Trump's mass deportation operations and immigration enforcement actions could reshape the way Texans vote. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez spoke with voters and officials about that.

item.title: El-Sayed, Rogers trade barbs at final Michigan Senate debate
item.description: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers went head-to-head during the Michigan Senate race's final debate on Wednesday night. CBS News White House and politics reporter Aaron Navarro joins with a recap.

item.title: Minnesota GOP Senate candidate Michele Tafoya on where she would break with Trump if elected
item.description: New polling shows Minnesota Republican Senate candidate Michele Tafoya making gains in her race against Democratic Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan. CBS News correspondent Jonah Kaplan spoke with Tafoya about how she would serve as a check on President Trump if elected to the Senate.

item.title: AOC teams up with Maine Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson for town hall
item.description: Democratic Senate nominee Troy Jackson held a town hall in Portland, Maine, on Thursday with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York. CBS News congressional reporter Taurean Small has the latest.

item.title: More people now use GLP-1s to lose weight than for other health issues
item.description: Growing usage of GLP-1 drugs for weight loss is reshaping how consumers shop for food and clothes, according to consulting firm EY-Parthenon.

item.title: DOJ investigating Corey Lewandowski over DHS role, sources say
item.description: The Justice Department is looking into allegations that Corey Lewandowski used his role at DHS for financial gain, sources told CBS News. Lewandowski has denied all wrongdoing.

item.title: GOP officials divided over Ramaswamy ad with Acton's mom
item.description: In the ad, which first circulated on social media Monday night, Democrat Amy Acton's estranged mother called her a liar.

item.title: Trump campaigning in ruby red area of Iowa with midterms 12 days away
item.description: President Trump is stumping for Republicans in Sioux City, Iowa, on Thursday, with 12 days until Election Day. CBS News chief Washington analyst Robert Costa is in the Hawkeye State with more.

item.title: Trump praises "powerful" Ramaswamy ad featuring Acton's mother
item.description: "Who wouldn't use such an Ad?" President Trump wrote. "I would, it's called, 'hitting pay dirt.'"

item.title: Ohio Republican Gov. DeWine urges Ramaswamy to take down Acton attack ad
item.description: Several Ohio Republicans on the ballot have come out against GOP gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad featuring the estranged mother of Amy Acton, his Democratic opponent. CBS News chief Washington correspondent Major Garrett has the details.

item.title: Michele Tafoya says Iran war has gone on "longer than I think people were ready for"
item.description: Some Republican candidates are vowing to break with President Trump on certain issues, including U.S. Senate candidate Michele Tafoya of Minnesota. CBS News correspondent Jonah Kaplan spoke with Tafoya as well as her opponent, Peggy Flanagan.

item.title: Trump reacts to controversial attack ad targeting Amy Acton and Musk's satellite slowdown in Ukraine
item.description: President Trump took questions from reporters outside the White House on Thursday, weighing in on Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy's attack ad featuring his opponent Amy Acton's estranged mother, as well as the revelation that Elon Musk chose to limit Ukraine's access to SpaceX's satellite service.

item.title: Public Service Loan Forgiveness overhaul dropped, filing shows
item.description: Advocates for student loan borrowers said the move will benefit workers who dedicate themselves to public service.

item.title: At least 16 dead when powerful 7.0 magnitude earthquake strikes Tibet
item.description: It was the biggest earthquake in the region in the last five years, China's national broadcaster CCTV said.

item.title: Tom Skerritt, known for roles in "Alien," "Picket Fences," dies at 93
item.description: Tom Skerritt died of natural causes, his family said in a statement.

item.title: Nasdaq dives 750 points as investors reassess AI spending
item.description: Investors are fretting over the massive debt AI companies are relying on to finance data center and chip spending, Wall Street analysts say.

item.title: Elon Musk's Starlink and Starshield, and what they mean to Ukraine
item.description: Here's what to know about Starlink and Starshield, the technologies Ukraine is relying on in the war against Russia.

item.title: DOJ didn't ensure school discrimination ended before dropping cases: watchdog
item.description: In at least 18 cases, the Justice Department supported dismissals without first asking the federal court overseeing the case to determine if the school had ended discriminatory practices.

item.title: What to know about the PHP bug affecting 70% of world's websites
item.description: AI was used to uncover a security weakness that affects most of the world's websites, researchers said. Here's what internet users should know.

item.title: Memphis fails to pass 1-year data center moratorium, opts for shorter-term ban
item.description: Memphis has become a hotspot for data centers driven by Elon Musk's SpaceXAI.

item.title: Hegseth bans use of nonpublic info for bets on U.S. military ops
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the ban applies to classified and unclassified information and includes prediction markets such as Polymarket and Kalshi.

item.title: Trump says Iran is making up strikes on ships to drive up oil prices
item.description: President Trump said Iran was trying to drive up oil prices before the midterms by lying about ships hitting mines or being struck by projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Judge curbs DHS efforts to conduct sweeps for possible noncitizen voters
item.description: A federal judge ruled DHS's practice of knocking on doors and asking people about their immigration status — and whether they have voted in recent elections — likely violates the Voting Rights Act.

item.title: Airbnb limits guest chores like laundry, drawing host backlash
item.description: The new policy prevents hosts from asking guests to strip beds, start a load of laundry and other tasks that "require significant effort or time."

item.title: Roller coaster safety experts weigh in on Six Flags investigation
item.description: The Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia has been closed since a man died after witnesses say he was ejected from the ride.

item.title: 10/20: CBS Evening News
item.description: A brake issue prompts an American Airlines emergency landing; Christina Applegate reveals a devastating misdiagnosis.

item.title: Illustrating myths: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opens
item.description: The art of illustrators, that tells mythic narratives and stories of our shared humanity, is at the core of a new Los Angeles institution: The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art, showcasing works featured in magazines, comics, fantasy stories, and motion picture design. CBS News' Norah O'Donnell talks with the museum's founders, George Lucas, the creator of "Star Wars," and his wife, businesswoman Mellody Hobson, about the emotional draw of storytelling art that shapes our world.

item.title: Southern California skincare store is accused of using coercive sales tactics
item.description: One claim alleges that a developmentally disabled man was pressured into spending more than $40,000 during a single visit and giving employees more than $10,000 in tips.
